V. Inordinate delay in passing an order about the liberty of a citizen is not in tune with the constitutional mandate, the
Supreme Court observed in an order allowing anticipatory bail plea. In this case, the High Court rejected the anticipatory
bail application filed by the accused. The Supreme Court granted him ad interim protection observing that (i) it was a
cross-case arising out of the civil dispute. (ii) Prima facie there was no material to show that the provisions of Scheduled
Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, were invoked. (iii) That there was a delay of six days in
lodging the FIR. In certain minor offences, it is the right of the accused to obtain bail while the trial is pending. These are
bailable offences. On the other hand, there are more serious offences where the accused do not have a right to obtain bail;
in such cases, bail can be granted only at the court's discretion. These are non-bailable offences. Certain offences are so
serious that any police officer can investigate and arrest an accused person without obtaining a warrant from a court. For
example, murder. These are cognizable offences. In other cases, the police must wait for the order of a magistrate before
investigating and arresting the accused. These are non-cognizable offences. In certain offences, the State which conducts
the prosecution and the accused can come to an arrangement where, instead of being imprisoned, the accused can pay a
fine. These are compoundable offences. In this case, the officer fining you is compounding your offence. Of course not all
offences are compoundable; it would not be desirable that murderers should be able to compound their offences.
The CrPC also provides that certain petty offences may be tried in a summary way. In a summary trial, no sentence of
imprisonment for a term exceeding three months can be passed in any conviction. If a fine of Rs. 200 or less is imposed in
such trials, then the accused has no right to appeal. A person may submit an anticipatory bail application if they believe
they will be detained by the police for an offence for which there is no possibility of bond. Before the hearing for the grant
of regular or anticipatory bail, a short-term bail is given to the accused. Such short-term bail is called ‘interim bail’.

VI. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 recognises acid attack victims as a category of persons entitled to
statutory protection, rehabilitation, and disability-related benefits. In Shaheen Malik v. Union of India & Anr. (2025),
the Supreme Court invoked its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to hold that the expression "acid attack
victim" must receive a purposive and beneficial interpretation. The Court held that the expression includes not only
persons disfigured by the throwing of acid but also persons who are forcibly made to consume acid and those who suffer
internal injuries caused by acid or similar corrosive substances, notwithstanding the absence of visible external
disfigurement. The Court directed that this interpretation shall operate retrospectively from the commencement of the
Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and urged the Union Government to suitably amend the Schedule appended
to the Act so as to remove the existing statutory lacuna. The Court observed that the legislative objective of the Act is to


protect every person who suffers disability as a consequence of an acid attack, irrespective of the manner in which the
injury is inflicted.
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 criminalises voluntarily causing injury by throwing, administering, or otherwise using
acid or any corrosive or burning substance. The offence includes causing permanent or partial damage, deformity,
maiming, disfigurement, disability, internal injuries, burn injuries, or rendering a person into a permanent vegetative state.
The offence is cognizable and non-bailable and is punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than ten years, which
may extend to imprisonment for life, together with a mandatory fine that is just, reasonable, and payable directly to the
victim for medical treatment and related expenses. Attempt to commit an acid attack constitutes a separate cognizable and

II. What is this emptiness and how to cope with it? This feeling of emptiness exists because our life is devoid of a deeper
meaning. If we peruse our existence from the very beginning till now, we will realize that we are simply following several
unwritten interpersonal, familial, social, religious, and cultural scripts and weaving our self around them. These schemas
influence our thoughts, feelings, strivings, likes, dislikes, and identities. They constantly whisper in our inner mental
space, telling us who we are, where do we belong, what we want and what we must do in our lives.
Hypothetically, if we were to remove ourselves from our given context and enter a completely different set of
circumstances in a different space, these scripts will change, and consequently our identity will also undergo
transformation. We will begin to think differently, feel differently and our desires, goals and aspirations will also change.
And yet the emptiness will remain because our old conditionings would be substituted by a new set of conditionings.
Once again, we will be wasting a lifetime pursuing insignificant goals without really understanding who we are and what
we really want.
The solution to this complex problem lies in breaking down our mental conditioning, figuring out our true self and letting
that profound inner knowledge steer our life. A deeper self-inquiry can help us in this journey. According to a certain
philosophy, “When one persistently enquires into the nature of the mind, the mind will end leaving the Self. What is
referred to as the Self is the Atman. When other thoughts arise, one should not pursue them, but should inquire: ‘To whom
do they arise?’ It does not matter how many thoughts arise. As each thought arises, one should inquire with diligence, ‘To
whom has this thought arisen?’ The answer that would emerge would be ‘To me.’ Thereupon if one asks ‘Who am I?’ the
mind will go back to its source; and the thought that arose will become quiescent. With repeated practice in this manner,
the mind will develop the skill to stay in its source.”
As we go deeper within, the narrow boundaries of our mind break, and we discover our true self and get connected to the
cosmic consciousness. Then, our life takes on a new significance and our old emptiness vanishes. No matter at what age
and stage of life we are, we can transform our existence by rethinking who we really are and start over.

philosophical-reflection-still-hold-value/

III. The technology is reaching heights day by day. On one side, we have advanced our technologies so much that most of
our work has become a piece of cake for us, but on the other side, it holds some worse sides too. Technology has become
both a boon and a bane for us. Particularly, the role of technology in modern-day crime is also evident. Committing a
crime and enforcement to investigate both has become easy. Through various mediums like phones, laptops, and iPads,
communication has become easy for criminals to execute crimes without being undetected.
Encrypted communication makes organized crimes harder to detect. In an encrypted format, messages are encoded in a
way that makes it difficult for law enforcers to decode them. Not only does it create difficulty in tracking these messages,
but it also happens in such a secretive way that this crime doesn’t caught easily. Furthermore, encrypted communications
not only make it difficult to track down the activities of criminals, but also make it harder to detect and track financial
transactions. If the data is not available, then it is difficult to follow the money flow, the person receiving it, and the source
of funding.


The online black market has gained popularity all over the world as it provides a place for anonymity. This market is the
same as the real-world market where the goods are sold against the jurisdiction of law. With the help of these websites,
people can buy or sell goods anonymously. Additionally, the delivery methods of these goods can be done through drones,
mail, and couriers. The payment is also done through cryptocurrencies like bitcoin which provides anonymity for buyers.
As we know social media has a significant role in our life. Cyberbullying is another serious issue that can lead to negative
impacts on people’s mental well-being. Through awareness and education about this issue can help to overcome it. It is
important to address this so that no other people become victims of these activities.
It is important to find the right balance between privacy and security. Organizations should keep this thing in mind to
secure people’s personal data or information and also respect their privacy. As these terms are used interchangeably.
Security is protecting individuals’ privacy. These privacy measures help people save data away from cyberattacks or being
stolen. On the other side privacy is a basic human right. Without their consent, it would be wrong to collect their data.
People and many organizations should provide transparency about how they are going to use your information without
any misuse. Lastly, people should be mindful while sharing any information.
Source: https://www.psychologs.com/virtual-heist-the-role-of-technology-in-modern-day-crime/

to the number of girls knowing Hindi?

content.passageText:
II. In a medical college there are 1600 students studying Dentistry and Homeopathy. Each student from each
course knows one or more languages out of English, Hindi and Bengali. 45% of the students study Dentistry
and the remaining students study Homeopathy.
Out of the students studying Dentistry, boys and girls are in the ratio of 5 : 3.
Out of the boys studying Dentistry, 16% know only English, 10% know only Hindi and 4% know only Bengali.
24% know English as well as Hindi, 20% know English as well as Bengali and 14% know Hindi as well as
Bengali. The remaining boys know all three languages.
Out of the girls studying Dentistry, 20% know only English, 10% know only Hindi and 10% know only
Bengali, 20% know English as well as Hindi, 20% know English as well as Bengali, 10% know Hindi as well as
Bengali. The remaining girls know all the three languages.
Out of the students studying Homeopathy, boys and girls are in the ratio of 4 : 7.
Out of the boys studying Homeopathy, 20% know only English, 15% know only Hindi and 5% know only
Bengali. 15% know English as well as Hindi, 25% know English as well as Bengali, and 10% know Hindi as
well as Bengali. The remaining boys know all three languages.
Out of the girls studying Homeopathy, 15% know only English, 15% know only Hindi and 5% know only
Bengali, 20% know English as well as Hindi, 20% know English as well as Bengali, and 15% know Hindi as
well as Bengali. The remaining girls know all three languages.
content.questionText:
What per cent of the total number of girls in the college do not know Hindi? (rounded off to nearest
integer)
